Subject: Request: regional dedicated pools for Q1 onboarding

Thanks for taking this — we have a Q1 rollout where we need guaranteed dedicated capacity in multiple regions. High-level asks:
- US: primary pool for production (initial steady state ~40-60 A100-equivalent GPUs, heavy burst windows during month-end)

Team — forwarding Markus’s ask. He explicitly called out tranche-based delivery tied to milestone payments. Initial thoughts below; please critique and update before I send the proposal.

Proposal sketch (v1):
- Phase 1 (Go-live, US primary): 40 A100-equivalent dedicated GPUs (serve steady traffic), configured with autoscale headroom to 80 for predictable month-end bursts. KV/prefix caching + batching expected to reduce token cost by ~20% in steady state.
- Phase 2 (Week 6 post-go-live, EU): 18 GPUs (lower baseline), with cross-region fallback to US if capacity constrained.
- Phase 3 (Month 3, APAC onramp): 10 GPUs initially; add 10 more on committed ramp at Month 3 if adoption > X DAU/throughput threshold.

Operational levers:
- Burst policy: allow short-term scaling to shared burst pool (best-effort) vs guaranteed reserved burst (contracted).
- Quantization profile: recommend int8 for non-critical endpoints to reduce GPU memory footprint where model quality allows.
- Monitoring SLA: per-route p99 latency SLO and token cost alerts.

Questions for sizing accuracy: expected tokens/sec per request, average request length, percent of calls that require p99 latency (low-latency vs batch).

Attached: q3_tranche_model_v1.xlsx (contains baseline utilization assumptions).

If we agree, I’ll (a) convert to pricing delta for reserved vs on-demand, (b) add lead times for regional provisioning (EU typically 4-6 weeks for private/VPC setups; APAC depends on region and partner, 6-10 weeks).

-Kim

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Request: regional dedicated pools for Q1 onboarding

Kim — good starting point. My adjustments based on recent infra telemetry and our committed pricing bands:
- Start US at 40 reserved GPUs, but configure autoscale to 80 with a 10-minute warmup window. This reduces immediate commit while covering burst risk.
- EU baseline 15 reserved + 5 burst-capable (effectively 20), rotate some capacity through smaller instances if legal/compliance needs prefer different SKU.
- APAC: 8 reserved, commit to add +8 at Month 3 trigger.

Assumptions I used (see attached capacity_estimates.csv):
- Token throughput per GPU: 25k tokens/minute steady, 60k tokens/minute burst (A100 profile, int8 when applicable).
- Average req token length: 150 tokens; p95 qps expected at 120 qps across US pool during month-end.

Cost levers: aggressive batching at the API gateway level and request-level cache TTLs give us quick wins. If they accept a 12-month reserved term, per-GPU unit cost drops ~18% vs month-to-month.

I’ll pull committed pricing numbers and add to the draft proposal.

-Neha

Hi Markus — per our internal sizing exercise (summary below) and following our call, please find a short proposal attached. Highlights:

Summary of recommended tranches:
- Phase 1 (US, go-live): 40 reserved GPUs with autoscale headroom to 80 for month-end burst. Expected steady p95 latency under SLO for critical routes.
- Phase 2 (EU, week 6): 15 reserved + 5 burst-capable; lead time for VPC/KMS provisioning: 4-6 weeks.
- Phase 3 (APAC, month 3 trigger): 8 reserved initial, +8 committed ramp at trigger. APAC lead time estimate: 6-10 weeks depending on partner region.

Commercial:
- 12-month reserved term recommended for meaningful per-GPU unit savings. We’ll share explicit reserved vs on-demand delta in the formal SOW.
- Burst policy options: best-effort shared burst pool (lower cost, no SLA) or contracted reserved burst (higher cost, guaranteed).

Action items (owner):
- FinTech Pros: fill usage profile in the attached QA checklist (Markus) — due EOD Mon 11/22.
- Redwood: deliver formal pricing + SOW with milestone-based tranches and DocuSign link (Kimberly) — targeted 11/24.
